description: A single black carpenter ant, climbing along the underside of a branch.
A thin, dark line of ants marching single-file along the top of a branch.
A cluster of tiny, pale green aphids, clinging to the soft underside of a young leaf.
A honeybee resting on a leaf, its legs heavy with pollen.
A bumblebee crawling slowly along a twig, its body vibrating with a low hum.
A small, iridescent beetle. Its shell shifts colors in the light.
A long, slender, green beetle. Its antennae wave as it walks along a branch.
A tiny, metallic, blue beetle, tucked into the angle where a twig meets a branch.
A small and dark cricket, sitting on a leaf.
A bright green katydid. Its wings are folded like leaves, perfectly camouflaged against the foliage.
A monarch butterfly, wings slowly opening and closing as it rests on a leaf.
A tiny, pale blue butterfly, fluttering between branches.
A small, jade-green chrysalis, studded with tiny gold flecks, hanging from a twig.
A fat, fuzzy caterpillar, banded in black and orange, inching along a branch.
A tiny, bright green caterpillar, nibbling a hole in a leaf.
A pale, hairless caterpillar, hanging from a twig on a single thread of silk.
A long, reddish-brown centipede, its many legs rippling as it disappears into a fork in the branches.
An empty, translucent, brown cicada shell, clinging to the underside of a branch.
A small, silky, pale brown cocoon, tucked into the crook of a twig.
A small, papery, brown egg case, attached to a twig like a tiny, ridged purse.
A round, white, papery egg sac, hanging from a branch by a thread of silk.
A single, iridescent bluebottle fly, resting on a leaf.
A small, green grasshopper, clinging to a branch with long, spindly legs.
A tiny, green inchworm, looping its way along the underside of a twig.
A bright red ladybug with seven black spots, resting on a leaf.
A cluster of small, orange ladybugs, huddled together in the crook of a branch.
A small, pale green praying mantis, perfectly still on a branch, its triangular head turned toward you.
A brown praying mantis, its forelegs raised, watching from the shadow of a leaf.
A small, dark, segmented millipede, curled into a tight spiral in the fork of two branches.
A large, pale moth with powdery wings, resting motionless on a branch.
A small, brown, intricately patterned moth, its wings folded flat against a twig.
A small, dark wolf spider, sitting motionless on a leaf.
A large, hairy, brown spider, its legs spanning the width of your palm, resting on a branch.
A small, perfect, dew-covered spiderweb, spun between two twigs, glittering in the light.
A tangled, dusty spiderweb, filling the space between branches, with a dried husk of a fly caught in it.
A long, single strand of spider silk, drifting from a branch in the breeze.
A single, yellow-and-black wasp, crawling slowly along a twig.
A small, papery wasp nest, hanging from a branch, its entrance guarded by a single, watchful wasp.
A small, grey, segmented woodlouse, curled into a tight, armored ball on a branch.
A small, brown, striped lizard, basking on a sunlit branch.
A small, green garden snake, coiled along a branch, watching you.
A small, cup-shaped nest, woven from twigs, moss, and soft grass, wedged into the fork of a branch.
A deep, soft nest, lined with feathers and fur, tucked into a hollow in the branches.
An old, weathered nest, its twigs brittle and broken, long since abandoned.
A small, perfect, blue egg, lying alone in a nest, speckled with brown.
A single, pale green egg, warm to the touch, resting in a bed of soft moss.
A broken, empty eggshell, its edges jagged, the inside dry and clean.
A single, soft, downy feather, caught in a twig.
A small cluster of downy feathers, nestled in the crook of a branch.
A small, brown, speckled feather, wedged into a fork in the branches.
A single, bright yellow feather, resting on a leaf.
A tiny, soft, grey feather, caught in a spiderweb between two branches.
A large, glossy, black feather, from a crow, wedged into a branch fork.
A long, grey-and-white striped feather, from a hawk, resting on a branch.
A large, blue-grey feather with a bold black tip, from a blue jay, lying on a leaf.
A long, elegant, white feather, from an owl, soft and silent.
A grey squirrel, perched on a branch, staring at you with bright, curious eyes.
A red squirrel, chattering at you from a high branch.
A large, messy ball of leaves and twigs, tucked into a fork in the branches. A squirrel's drey.
A single, small, hard, brown nut, wedged into the crook of a branch.
A cracked, empty hazelnut shell, resting on a branch.
A single, shiny, brown chestnut, resting on a leaf.
A small pile of acorns, carefully gathered in a fork in the branches.
A single, perfect acorn, still in its cap, resting on a twig.
An empty acorn cap, lying on a branch, its edges frilled.
A round, hard, brown growth on a branch, about the size of a small plum.
A cluster of small, round galls, growing on the underside of a leaf.
A single, dry, curled leaf, caught in a fork in the branches.
A fresh, green leaf, still attached to its twig, trembling in the breeze.
A single, brilliant red leaf, resting on a branch.
A pale, translucent, skeletonized leaf, its fleshy parts eaten away, leaving only a delicate framework.
A single, enormous, broad leaf, draped over a branch like a small canopy.
A cluster of tiny, new leaves, unfurling from a bud at the tip of a twig.
A single, yellow leaf, still clinging to its twig, the only one left.
A single, tight, green bud, resting at the tip of a twig, waiting.
A cluster of small, pink buds, about to bloom.
A single, perfect, pink blossom, resting on a branch.
A small cluster of white blossoms, fragrant and soft.
A single, fallen blossom, resting on a leaf, its petals slightly wilted.
A single, tiny, purple flower, growing directly from the bark of a branch.
A small cluster of ripe, dark berries, hanging from a twig.
A single, perfect, red berry, resting on a branch.
A thin, dry, forked twig, broken off and resting in a fork.
A small, fresh, green twig, snapped off and lying on a branch.
A single, perfectly straight twig, about a foot long, resting on a branch.
A long, thin, flexible twig, curved into a graceful arch.
A small, straight, dry stick, about the length of a finger, wedged into a fork in the branches.
A long, curved walking stick, leaning against a branch as if someone left it behind.
A forked stick, sharpened at one end, wedged into the branches, a crudely carved 'R' on the handle.
A small, soft patch of green moss, growing on the top of a branch.
A tiny, perfect cushion of star-shaped moss, growing in a fork in the branches.
A patch of pale, silvery-green lichen, crusting a branch in a ruffled pattern.
A bright orange lichen, growing in a perfect circle on a branch.
A beard-like tangle of grey-green lichen, hanging from a branch in wispy strands.
A pale, powdery blue-grey lichen, dusting a branch like fine frost.
A small, pale, shelf-like fungus growing out of the underside of a branch.
A cluster of tiny, bright orange fungi, growing in a neat row along a branch.
A single, large, bracket fungus, banded in brown and cream, growing from the side of a branch.
A single, golden drop of sap, oozing from a crack in a branch.
A long, dried trail of amber-colored sap, running down the side of a branch like a frozen tear.
A hard, golden, translucent lump of resin, resting in a fork in the branches.
A sticky, fresh blob of resin, oozing from a wound in the bark.
A single, winged maple seed, caught in a fork in the branches.
A tiny, hard, black seed, resting on a leaf.
A single, fluffy, cotton-like seed, caught in a twig.
A long, dry, brown seed pod, hanging from a branch, rattling in the wind.
A small, round, spiky seed ball, hanging from a twig.
A tiny, spiral snail shell, empty and dry, wedged into a fork in the branches.
A small, smooth, white shell, resting in the crook of a branch. It looks out of place this high up.
A single, smooth, blue glass marble, wedged into a fork in the branches.
A small, chipped, white marble, resting on a branch.
A tiny, perfectly round, blue glass bead, resting on a leaf.
A small, round, wooden button, carved with a pattern of leaves, resting on a branch.
A single, ornate brass button, tarnished green with age, wedged into a fork.
A small, tarnished copper coin, wedged into a crack in a branch.
A silver coin, resting on a branch, a tiny star scratched into its face.
A single, ancient gold coin, resting in the fork of two branches.
A tiny, brass coin with a hole punched through the center, threaded on a dried leather cord that hangs from a twig.
A long, faded, red ribbon, tied around a branch, its ends frayed and waving in the breeze.
A thin, blue ribbon, tied in a neat bow around a twig.
A small, faded scrap of fabric, caught on a twig, fluttering in the wind.
A torn piece of plaid cloth, snagged on a branch. It looks like it was once part of a shirt.
A long, thin piece of twine, tied to a branch, its other end trailing off into the foliage.
A single strand of red thread, tied around a twig in a small, careful knot.
A thick, weathered rope, tied to a sturdy branch, a wooden seat hanging at its end.
A frayed, old rope, tied to a branch, its wooden seat long since rotted away. Only a single, empty loop remains.
A small, delicate wind chime, made of shells and driftwood, hanging from a branch.
A simple wind chime, made of hollow bamboo tubes, hanging from a branch, clacking softly in the breeze.
A small, woven dreamcatcher, made of twigs and sinew, decorated with feathers and beads, hanging from a branch.
A small, weathered dreamcatcher, its web torn, its feathers faded and grey. It has been here a long time.
A small note, tied to a twig with a strand of grass. It reads: 'I climbed this high and all I got was this note.'
A tiny note, pinned to a leaf with a thorn: 'The view from up here is amazing. You should climb more trees.'
A small note, folded and tucked into a fork: 'If you're reading this, you're probably stuck. I was too. Good luck.'
A note, tied to a branch with a faded ribbon: 'I left this here for someone to find. I hope that someone is you.'
A tiny note, rolled up and tucked into a bud: 'The bees are plotting. They have tiny hats. It is very concerning.'
A small note, tucked into a squirrel's drey: 'Dear squirrel, I borrowed one acorn. I will pay you back with interest. Sincerely, a hungry traveler.'
A scrap of paper, wedged into a fork: 'I once saw a bear climb this tree. It did not go well. Do not tell the bear I told you.'
A note, written in very shaky handwriting: 'I am writing this from the top of this tree. I am afraid of heights. I do not know how I got here.'
A note, written in a careful, neat hand: 'If you find this note, please add your own. Leave it for the next traveler.'
A note, written in a child's handwriting: 'I saw a bird up here. It was very small. It had a lot of opinions.'
A note, tied to a twig with a piece of thread: 'I am writing this note to remind myself to stop writing notes. This is the last one. Probably.'
A note, on a scrap of birch bark: 'I came up here to think. I thought about lunch. Mission accomplished.'
A small note, tucked into a knot: 'To whoever finds this: the answer is still 42. You're still welcome.'
A note, written in careful, elegant script: 'A bird once landed on my hand while I sat in this tree. I have never been the same since.'
A note, written in berry juice, faded: 'The stars are beautiful from up here. Wait for nightfall.'
A note, written in very small letters: 'If you are reading this, you have climbed higher than most. I am proud of you.'
A sad little note, written in shaky ink: 'I came here to say goodbye to someone. The tree was kind. I feel a little better now.'
A sweet note, written in careful cursive: 'I carved our initials into this branch. If you find this, know that I still think of you.'
A note, written in looping script: 'Whoever finds this note is now obligated to climb one branch higher. Do it. It's worth it.'
A note, tucked into a fork, written in a trembling hand: 'I was here. I was scared. But I climbed. And I am proud.'
A small, smooth stone that glows with a soft, steady pink light. Birds are fond of them and often carry them to their nests.
A small, smooth stone that glows with a cool, gentle blue light. Birds are fond of them and often carry them to their nests.
A small, smooth stone that glows with a warm, mossy green light. Birds are fond of them and often carry them to their nests.
A small, smooth stone that glows with a rich, amber light, like a tiny lantern. Birds are fond of them and often carry them to their nests.
A small, smooth stone that shifts slowly through every color of the rainbow. Birds are fond of them and often carry them to their nests.
A small cluster of glowstones, wedged into a fork of the branches. Each one pulses in a different color, as if quietly speaking to the others.
A single, silver-white flower that only opens at night. It folds shut at the first touch of dawn.
A small cluster of moonpetals, all glowing softly in the dark, their petals like flakes of moonlight.
A fragment of dark, impossibly thin bark that shows a moving constellation across its surface when held up to the sky.
A small, smooth piece of dark wood, warm to the touch, with tiny points of light drifting slowly across its face like stars.
A small, pale leaf that repeats back, in a whisper, whatever is spoken near it.
A cluster of pale leaves, all whispering to one another in a language you almost understand.
A small, papery pod hanging from a twig, glowing with a soft, golden light. It sways gently, even when there is no wind.
Three small, papery pods, each glowing a different color, hanging together like tiny lanterns.
A knot in the wood that hums a single note when the wind passes through it. Every knot hums a different note.
A row of hollow knots along a branch, each one humming its own note, together forming a slow, wandering melody.
A frozen dewdrop, perfectly clear, that never melts. It feels cool and hums faintly when touched.
A string of frozen dewdrops, threaded along a strand of spider silk, chiming together in the breeze.
A strip of bark with faint, glowing runes carved into it. The runes shift slowly, spelling words in a language you almost recognize.
A small, curled fragment of bark, covered in glowing runes that pulse in time with your heartbeat.
A small, pale egg that hums a soft, wordless song. It grows warmer when you hold it.
A clutch of small, pale eggs, humming together in a slow, sleepy harmony.
A single strand of silk, fine as spider's thread, that shimmers with faint, shifting colors. It feels like it remembers being dreamt.
A tangle of dream-silk strands, snagged on a branch, glowing softly and humming with quiet, half-formed images.
A single leaf that glows like a live ember. It is warm to the touch but never burns, and never cools.
A cluster of ember-leaves, all glowing together in the shade, as if the branch itself is on fire.
A small acorn that glows with a soft, silver light. It is cool to the touch and feels heavier than it should.
A small, clear crystal that hums a single, perfect note. The note changes with the seasons.
A blackened twig, its leaves burned away. It snaps at the slightest touch.
A nut with its shell charred and cracked. The meat inside is dry and bitter.
A leaf that survived the fire but is stained dark with soot. It is brittle and smells of woodsmoke.
A single leaf, its edges glowing faintly like an ember. It never burns away, but never cools either.
A ribbon, its colors faded and its edges singed. It still hangs from its branch, waiting for someone who will not return.
An egg, its shell cracked and blackened. Whatever was inside did not survive.
A nest, its twigs charred and its lining burned away. It has not been used since the fire.
A feather, blackened at the tips but unburned at the quill. It smells of smoke.
A glowstone, dimmed to a deep ember-red by fire, tucked into a branch fork. It never fully cools.
A note that survived the fire. It reads: 'The tree will come back. It always comes back. So will we.'
A ribbon, tied to a branch, that survived the strike. Its color has shifted to a strange, shifting silver-blue.
A branch split cleanly in two by the strike, both halves still hanging on. They hum faintly when the wind blows.
A leaf that crackles faintly when touched, as if still holding the charge of the storm.
A note that survived the strike. The ink has been scorched into patterns that look almost like runes, spelling a word you almost recognize.
A bird's nest that was in the tree when lightning struck. The eggs inside are warm and humming, but no bird has returned.
An acorn that absorbed the strike. It is hot to the touch and crackles when shaken. If you plant it, the tree it grows might be different.
A small loop of fused glass, formed from a vine and the sand around it in the instant of the strike. It fits a wrist perfectly.
A small crystal, formed where the lightning struck a branch. It hums a single, clear note and glows a pale blue.
A glowstone that was in the branches when lightning struck. It is now white-gold and fiercely bright. Birds will not touch this one.
A note still tied to its branch. It reads: 'I climbed this tree to hear the sky better. It spoke loud enough for the both of us.'
